                          YATES’S INITIAL BRIEF
               TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES

       COMES NOW Intervenor John Griffin Yates, Jr. ("Yates") and respectfully submits this

Initial Brief in opposition to Route 894 and any route utilizing Links J12, J13, J14, J25, J27, and

J4 (hereinafter, “Yates Links”). If the Commission determines a route crossing the Yates’s

property is necessary, the Commission should select Route 487. While Route 487 utilizes Links

J12 and J13, it is the route with the least adverse consequences as it minimizes the negative impact

to the Yates’s property.

       I.      INTRODUCTION

       This proceeding concerns the routing of the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation

765-KV transmission line project across Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason,

McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, and Williamson counties

(the "Project''). Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services




PUC DOCKET NO. 59475; SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349; YATES’S INITIAL BRIEF
TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES
PAGE 1 OF 10
 Corporation (collectively, ''Applicants") seek approval of the Project.1 Yates owns approximately

3,231 acres in San Saba County, Texas (hereinafter, “Yates’s Property”). Numerous proposed

route configurations traverse the Yates’s Property through use of the Yates Links. Yates seeks to

minimize the negative impacts to his property and future use of land.

        The record demonstrates three preferred routes of interest: 894, 891, and 487 (hereinafter,

“Preferred Routes of Interest”). However, Yates believes that Applicants’ Route of Interest 296

best satisfies the Commission’s routing criteria (hereinafter, “Yates Preferred Route”). Route 296

is comparable in both length and cost to the Preferred Routes of Interest, and Route 296 avoids

unnecessary and wholly avoidable impacts on the Yates’s Property.

        In the alternative, while Yates prefers Route 296 to the other routes of interest, Yates finds

that Route 487 is less materially damaging than Routes 894 and 891. The evidence demonstrates

that routes utilizing Links J4, J25, and J27, such as Routes 894 and 891, impose substantially

greater impacts on the Yates’s Property than routes utilizing Links J12 and J13, such as Route 487.

Accordingly, if the Commission determines that a route crossing the Yates’s Property is necessary,

it should avoid utilizing Links J4, J25, and J27, and instead select Route 487 to minimize impact

to the Yates’s Property and best satisfy the Commission’s routing criteria.

        II.      LEGAL STANDARD

        The Commission must determine which route best satisfies the routing criteria established

by statute and rule.2 Under PURA §37.056(c), the Commission must consider several factors when

evaluating transmission line routes, including community values, recreational and park areas,

historic and aesthetic values, environmental integrity, and the probable improvement of service or

 lowering of costs to consumers.3 Transmission lines should be routed to moderate impacts on the

affected community and landowners to the extent reasonable, unless the Applicants show that grid

reliability and security dictate otherwise.4

        In evaluating alternative routes, the Commission considers a variety of factors, including

route length, estimated project and life-cycle cost, the use of compatible rights-of-way, and

impacts on habitable structures, land use, agricultural operations, the environment, economic

activity, and affected landowners.5 No single routing factor is dispositive.6 Rather, the Commission

must weigh all routing considerations together and determine which route best satisfies the

applicable statutory and regulatory criteria.7 The Applicants bear the burden of demonstrating their

proposed route best balances the relevant factors.8 Where the record shows that an alternative route

more effectively minimizes impacts to the protected routing interests, while remaining reasonable

from an engineering and cost perspective, the Commission should reject the Applicants’ proposed

route in favor of the superior alternative.9

        III.    THE PREFERRED ROUTES OF INTEREST WOULD SIGNIFICANTLY
                IMPACT THE YATES’S PROPERTY


        Applicants have submitted eight routes of interest.10 These include Routes 296, 392, 410,

487, 572, 891, 894, and Cherokee G. The Preferred Routes of Interest include Routes 487, 891,

and 894. Yates’s Preferred Route is Route 296.

        A. Preferred Route of Interest 891

        Route 891 is a high impact route that unnecessarily concentrates on the Yates’s Property.

It directly uses Links J27 and J4, has a much longer and circuitous route, while converging on the

same corridor as Route 894.12 Route 891 imposes some of the most significant impacts of any

route under consideration because Links J27 and J4 bisect Yates’s property, affect the Highway

16 frontage, interfere with access, and are in close proximity to the old homestead on the property

and the location of Yates’s planned retirement home.13 Route 891 causes avoidable intrusion into

the Yates’s Property and Applicants have not met their burden in establishing the necessity for this

preferred route.

          B. Preferred Route of Interest 894

         Route 894 is another high impact route that unnecessarily concentrates on the Yates’s

Property. It converges on the same corridor as Route 891, making it functionally equivalent in

terms of property impact, but adds unnecessary routing complexity through the addition of the H

Links without reducing impacts on landowners.14 Similar to Route 891, Route 894 also utilizes

Links J27 and J4, which bisect the Yates’s Property, affect the Highway 16 frontage, interfere with

access, and are in close proximity to the old homestead on the property and the location of Yates’s

planned retirement home.15 Here again, Route 894 causes avoidable intrusion into the Yates’s

Property and Applicants have not met their burden in establishing the necessity for this preferred

route.

         C. Preferred Route of Interest 487

         Of the three preferred routes, Route 487 is least materially damaging to the Yates’s

Property. Route 487 does not utilize Links J27 and J4 and instead uses a southern/central approach

that has a more direct transition into the K Links.16 This route still impacts Yates as it utilizes Links

J12/J13 (which infringe upon the Yates’s Property) but it offers a much lower impact. Furthermore,

as Route 487 is one of the main Preferred Routes of Interest, it undermines any claim by Applicant

that using Links J27/J4, and by extension Routes 894 and 891, is necessary for this project.

         D. Yates’s Ideal Route of Interest 296

     Intervenor believes that Route of Interest 296 is most ideal. Through this route, the Yates Links

are entirely avoided while maintaining a viable and efficient transmission path for the project.17 It

 maintains geographic feasibility while maintaining network continuity to the same K Link

     IV.      YATES OPPOSES THE USE OF ROUTES 891 AND 894

           Applicants have not met their burden in demonstrating Routes 891, 894, and 487 satisfy

statutory and regulatory criteria and best balance the relevant factors.19 The existence of Route 487

and Route 296 demonstrates viable alternatives to the use of Links J27 and J4 in Routes 891 and

894, and yet Applicants’ preferred routes are Routes 891 and 894. These not only have a high

overall impact due to their use of Links J27 and J4, but they are non-essential and fail to meet the

routing criteria when alternative routes such as Routes 296 and 487 exist.

           Under 16 Texas Administrative Code §25.101(b)(3)(B), the Commission is required to

consider whether proposed routes parallel or utilize existing compatible rights-of-way, including

roads, highways, telephone utilities and railroads, or parallel property lines or other natural or

cultural features, when evaluating transmission line routing alternatives.20 As Routes 894 and 891

utilize Links J27 and J4, they would effectively divide the approximately 3,231-acre ranch into

northern and southern portions, creating a permanent transmission corridor through the property.

This configuration would interfere with ranch operations, disrupt cattle grazing, reduce usable

hunting areas and diminish hunting activities, while simultaneously destroying the property’s

visual character and usability. Link J4 also runs along a substantial portion of the property’s

Highway 16 frontage. As a result, access to portions of the property would require traveling

beneath the transmission line, creating a permanent burden on ingress and egress as well as altering

the appearance of the property for lessees and hunting guests.

            Furthermore, the intersection of Links J4, J25, and J27 is very close to the old homestead

located on the southern section of the property and the site where Yates intends to build his

retirement home. Routes 891 and 894 would impact portions of the property with personal and

future residential significance. For these reasons, Yates strictly opposes the preferred routes of

interest 891 and 894.


     V.       ROUTE OF INTEREST 487 IS THE LEAST MATERIALLY DAMAGING
              ROUTE OF ALL THE PREFERRED ROUTES OF INTEREST

           Routes 891 and 894 are among the least reasonable alternatives because they require use

of the J27/J4 link corridor that directly impacts the Yates’s Property. Applicants’ inclusion of

Route 487 demonstrates the project can be successfully routed without utilizing Links J27 and J4.

Route 487 utilizes Links J12 and J13.21 These Links are located near the northern portion of the

property and are situated closer to existing infrastructure on the property. Most importantly, Route

487 avoids the route configuration that would divide the ranch into northern and southern portions

and avoids the substantial impacts to the property’s Highway 16 frontage that result from Link J4

and does not place transmission facilities in the same proximity to the site of Yates’s planned

retirement home. As a result, Route 487 would be less disruptive to the overall use and enjoyment

of Yates’s property and is materially less damaging to the property than Routes 894 and 891.

           Thus, while Yates prefers selection of a route that avoids the Yates’s Property entirely, if

the Commission determines that a route crossing the Yates’s Property is necessary, Route 487

represents the least detestable option.


     VI.      ROUTE OF INTEREST 296 EFFECTIVELY MINIMIZES IMPACTS TO THE
              PROTECTED ROUTING INTERESTS

            Route of Interest 296 demonstrates that avoidance of the Yates’s Property is not only

feasible but practical within the existing routing framework and project considerations. Route of

Interest 296 is the most ideal routing option because it maintains a continuous and operationally

viable transmission path, while presenting a more reasonable engineering approach than

Applicants’ preferred routes. Rather than forcing the project through high-impact residential and

ranch corridors, such as the Yates’s Property, Route of Interest 296 utilizes Links J31/J32/J33/J6.

This route still uses the J Links and preserves continuity into the K Links, without imposing

unnecessary burdens on any single property owner.

           Unlike the Preferred Routes, Route 296 does not utilize any of the Yates Links and does

not fragment Yates’s Property. Route of Interest 296 avoids transmission infrastructure near the

Highway 16 frontage, avoids bifurcation of the ranch into northern and southern halves, and avoids

placing potentially dangerous transmission facilities near the old homestead and planned

retirement home.22


       VII.     CONCLUSION

           The existence of Route of Interest 296 undermines any assertion that impacts to the Yates’s

Property are necessary or unavoidable in order to achieve project objectives. Route of Interest 296

allows for the complete avoidance of the Yates’s Property, while also balancing the routing

considerations. The record demonstrates that Applicants’ Preferred Routes of Interest 894 and 891

would place the transmission line across the Yates’s Property in a manner that impairs the

property’s use, character, and future development. These routes are burdensome because they

affect the Highway 16 frontage, bisect the ranch, and encroach upon existing and future planned


22
     Direct Testimony of John Griffin Yates, Jr. at 3-7.

 infrastructure. Likewise, Applicants’ Preferred Route of Interest 487 still negatively impacts the

Yates’s Property, however it is materially less damaging to the property than Routes 894 and 891.

       The evidence shows that the Applicants’ Preferred Routes demonstrate unnecessary and

avoidable impacts on the Yates’s Property. Accordingly, the Commission should approve Route

296 as the route that best meets the statutory and regulatory criteria and reject any route utilizing

the Yates Links. If the Commission finds it necessary to choose among the Applicants’ Preferred

Routes, the Commission should approve Route 487 as it is the least materially damaging to the

Yates’s Property.

    IV.        YATES OPPOSES THE USE OF ROUTES 891 AND 894

          Applicants have not met their burden in demonstrating Routes 891, 894, and 487 satisfy

statutory and regulatory criteria and best balance the relevant factors.19 The existence ofRoute 487

and Route 296 demonstrates viable alternatives to the use of Links J27 and J4 in Routes 891 and

894, and yet Applicants' preferred routes are Routes 891 and 894. These not only have a high

overall impact due to their use of Links J27 and J4, but they are non-essential and fail to meet the

routing criteria when alternative routes such as Routes 296 and 487 exist.

          Under 16 Texas Administrative Code §25.101(b)(3)(B), the Commission is required to

consider whether proposed routes parallel or utilize existing compatible rights-of-way, including

roads, highways, telephone utilities and railroads, or parallel property lines or other natural or

cultural features, when evaluating transmission line routing alternatives.20 As Routes 894 and 891

utilize Links J27 and J4, they would effectively divide the approximately 3,23 1-acre ranch into

northern and southern portions, creating a permanent transmission corridor through the property.

This configuration would interfere with ranch operations, disrupt cattle grazing, reduce usable

hunting areas and diminish hunting activities, while simultaneously destroying the property' s

visual character and usability. Link J4 also runs along a substantial portion of the property' s

Highway 16 frontage. As a result, access to portions of the property would require traveling

beneath the transmission line, creating a permanent burden on ingress and egress as well as altering

the appearance of the property for lessees and hunting guests.

    V.       ROUTE OF INTEREST 487 IS THE LEAST MATERIALLY DAMAGING
             ROUTE OF ALL THE PREFERRED ROUTES OF INTEREST

          Routes 891 and 894 are among the least reasonable alternatives because they require use

of the J27/J4 link corridor that directly impacts the Yates' s Property. Applicants' inclusion of

Route 487 demonstrates the project can be successfully routed without utilizing Links J27 and J4.

Route 487 utilizes Links J12 and J13.21 These Links are located near the northern portion of the

property and are situated closer to existing infrastructure on the property. Most importantly, Route

487 avoids the route configuration that would divide the ranch into northern and southern portions

and avoids the substantial impacts to the property' s Highway 16 frontage that result from Link J4

and does not place transmission facilities in the same proximity to the site of Yates' s planned

retirement home. As a result, Route 487 would be less disruptive to the overall use and enjoyment

of Yates' s property and is materially less damaging to the property than Routes 894 and 891.

          Thus, while Yates prefers selection of a route that avoids the Yates's Property entirely, if

the Commission determines that a route crossing the Yates's Property is necessary, Route 487

represents the least detestable option.
